chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his forefathers (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'Which charity is superior?' He replied, 'Giving charity to the stingy relative.'
ai.seo_question: What is the best type of charity according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) identifies charity to a stingy relative as the most superior form of Sadaqah, emphasizing the dual virtue of *Sadaqah* (charity) and *Silat al-Rahim* (maintaining kinship ties). Shia scholars highlight that giving to a *Kashih* (stingy person) is particularly meritorious because it combines financial generosity with the patience required to sustain family bonds despite their reluctance or difficulty, thereby strengthening the social fabric of the community.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 18. Abi (rah) from Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) from his forefathers (a.s.) who said:

Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his predecessors that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) was asked, “Which Sadaqah is better?” The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) replied, “Giving Sadaqah to an inimical relative.”
